cards.front: What starts each of the three complement pathways, and where do they meet?
cards.back: **Classical**: C1q binds **IgG or IgM** in antigen-antibody complexes. **Lectin**: **mannose-binding lectin** binds sugars on microbes. **Alternative**: **spontaneous C3 hydrolysis** in plasma; the C3b sticks to microbes, which lack host regulators. All three form a **C3 convertase**, which cleaves C3 into C3a and C3b.
cards.back_pt: **Clássica**: o C1q se liga a **IgG ou IgM** em complexos antígeno-anticorpo. **Lectinas**: a **lectina ligadora de manose** se liga a açúcares de micro-organismos. **Alternativa**: **hidrólise espontânea do C3** no plasma; o C3b se fixa aos micro-organismos, que não têm reguladores do hospedeiro. As três formam uma **C3 convertase**, que cliva o C3 em C3a e C3b.

cards.front: What are the main effector functions of C3b, C3a/C5a and C5b-9?
cards.back: **C3b**: **opsonin**; coats microbes so phagocytes can bind and eat them, and helps clear immune complexes. **C3a and C5a**: **anaphylatoxins** that make mast cells release histamine; **C5a** also attracts **neutrophils**. **C5b-9**: **membrane attack complex**, which forms pores and lyses cells.
cards.back_pt: **C3b**: **opsonina**; recobre micro-organismos para que os fagócitos os reconheçam e fagocitem, e ajuda a remover imunocomplexos. **C3a e C5a**: **anafilatoxinas** que fazem os mastócitos liberarem histamina; o **C5a** também atrai **neutrófilos**. **C5b-9**: **complexo de ataque à membrana**, que forma poros e lisa células.

cards.front: Which clinical pattern goes with each group of complement deficiencies?
cards.back: **Early classical (C1q, C2, C4)**: **lupus-like** immune-complex disease (C2 also: encapsulated infections). **C3**: severe, recurrent **pyogenic infections** with encapsulated bacteria. **Terminal (C5-C9)**: recurrent ***Neisseria*** infections. **C1 inhibitor**: **hereditary angioedema**.
cards.back_pt: **Clássica inicial (C1q, C2, C4)**: doença por imunocomplexos **semelhante ao lúpus** (C2 também: infecções por encapsuladas). **C3**: **infecções piogênicas** graves e recorrentes por bactérias encapsuladas. **Terminal (C5-C9)**: infecções recorrentes por ***Neisseria***. **Inibidor de C1**: **angioedema hereditário**.

cards.front: What does the NLRP3 inflammasome do?
cards.back: It is a cytoplasmic sensor of danger signals (for example, **urate crystals**). It activates **caspase-1**, which cuts **pro-IL-1β** (and pro-IL-18) into active cytokines and can cause an inflammatory cell death called **pyroptosis**.
cards.back_pt: É um sensor citoplasmático de sinais de perigo (por exemplo, **cristais de urato**). Ativa a **caspase-1**, que cliva a **pró-IL-1β** (e a pró-IL-18) nas citocinas ativas e pode causar uma morte celular inflamatória chamada **piroptose**.

cards.front: How do NK cells decide which cells to kill?
cards.back: NK cells (**CD56+, CD16+**, CD3-) kill cells that lack **MHC class I** ("**missing self**"), such as some virus-infected and tumor cells. They also kill IgG-coated cells by **ADCC** through CD16. They use **perforin and granzymes** and need no prior sensitization.
cards.back_pt: As células NK (**CD56+, CD16+**, CD3-) matam células sem **MHC de classe I** (***missing self***, "ausência do próprio"), como algumas células infectadas por vírus e células tumorais. Também matam células recobertas por IgG por **ADCC** via CD16. Usam **perforina e granzimas** e não precisam de sensibilização prévia.

cards.front: Which cytokine drives the hepatic acute-phase response, and which proteins rise or fall?
cards.back: Mainly **IL-6**. **Rise**: **CRP**, **ferritin**, **fibrinogen** (raises the ESR), **hepcidin**, serum amyloid A and haptoglobin. **Fall** (negative reactants): **albumin** and **transferrin**.
cards.back_pt: Principalmente a **IL-6**. **Aumentam**: **PCR**, **ferritina**, **fibrinogênio** (eleva a VHS), **hepcidina**, amiloide A sérico e haptoglobina. **Diminuem** (reagentes negativos): **albumina** e **transferrina**.

cards.back: **Endogenous pyrogens** (**IL-1**, **IL-6**, **TNF-α**) reach the hypothalamus and induce **COX-2**. Local **PGE2** raises the **thermoregulatory set point**. NSAIDs block COX everywhere; **acetaminophen** blocks it mainly in the brain, so it lowers fever with little anti-inflammatory effect.
cards.back_pt: Os **pirógenos endógenos** (**IL-1**, **IL-6**, **TNF-α**) chegam ao hipotálamo e induzem a **COX-2**. A **PGE2** local eleva o **ponto de ajuste termorregulador**. Os AINEs bloqueiam a COX em todo o corpo; o **paracetamol** a bloqueia principalmente no cérebro, por isso reduz a febre com pouco efeito anti-inflamatório.

cards.front: How do type I interferons (IFN-α and IFN-β) protect nearby cells from a virus?
cards.back: Virus-infected cells release them. Neighboring cells then make enzymes that **block viral protein synthesis** (PKR) and **degrade RNA** (RNase L): the **antiviral state**. Type I interferons also increase **MHC class I** expression and activate **NK cells**.
cards.back_pt: São liberados por células infectadas por vírus. As células vizinhas passam a produzir enzimas que **bloqueiam a síntese de proteínas virais** (PKR) e **degradam o RNA** (RNase L): o **estado antiviral**. Os interferons do tipo I também aumentam a expressão de **MHC de classe I** e ativam as **células NK**.

questions.stem: A 20-year-old man is admitted with fever, neck stiffness and a petechial rash. Cerebrospinal fluid shows many neutrophils and gram-negative diplococci. Three years ago he had another episode of meningococcal meningitis. He has never had pneumonia, sinusitis or ear infections, and he has no joint pain or rash between episodes. Serum IgG, IgA and IgM levels are normal. The total hemolytic complement activity (CH50) is undetectable. A deficiency of which protein is most likely?
questions.explanation: Recurrent ***Neisseria*** infection with an undetectable CH50 points to a **terminal complement (C5-C8) deficiency**, because the **membrane attack complex** is needed to lyse these bacteria. A **C3** deficiency also lowers CH50, but it causes severe recurrent pyogenic infections such as pneumonia and sinusitis, which he has never had. C2 deficiency usually presents with lupus-like disease.
questions.explanation_pt: Infecção recorrente por ***Neisseria*** com CH50 indetectável indica **deficiência do complemento terminal (C5-C8)**, pois o **complexo de ataque à membrana** é necessário para lisar essas bactérias. A deficiência de **C3** também reduz o CH50, mas causa infecções piogênicas graves e recorrentes, como pneumonia e sinusite, que ele nunca teve. A deficiência de C2 costuma se manifestar como doença semelhante ao lúpus.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman has had episodes of swelling of the lips, hands and face since adolescence. Some episodes come with crampy abdominal pain and vomiting. Each episode lasts 2 to 3 days. The current episode began the day after a tooth extraction. She has no itching and no hives, and antihistamines have never helped. Her father has similar episodes. Exam shows non-pitting swelling of the lips without wheals. Which set of laboratory results is most likely?
choices: Low C4, normal C3, low C1 inhibitor function
Low C3, normal C4, normal C1 inhibitor function
Low C3 and low C4, normal C1 inhibitor function
Normal C3 and C4, elevated serum tryptase
Normal C3 and C4, undetectable CH50
questions.explanation: This is **hereditary angioedema** (autosomal dominant **C1 inhibitor** deficiency). Without the inhibitor, C1 keeps cleaving **C4**, so C4 is low while **C3 is normal**; kallikrein is also uncontrolled, so **bradykinin** causes the swelling. Elevated tryptase points to mast cell activation (anaphylaxis), which brings itching, hives and a response to antihistamines. Low C3 and C4 together suggest immune-complex disease such as lupus.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **angioedema hereditário** (deficiência autossômica dominante do **inibidor de C1**). Sem o inibidor, o C1 continua clivando o **C4**, que fica baixo enquanto o **C3 permanece normal**; a calicreína também fica sem controle, e a **bradicinina** causa o edema. Triptase elevada indica ativação de mastócitos (anafilaxia), que traz prurido, urticas e resposta a anti-histamínicos. C3 e C4 baixos juntos sugerem doença por imunocomplexos, como o lúpus.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man has metastatic melanoma. Analysis of his tumor shows a mutation in the β2-microglobulin gene, so the tumor cells have no MHC class I molecules on their surface. In the laboratory, his tumor cells are mixed with white blood cells from his own blood. The tumor cells are killed within hours, without any prior exposure of the white blood cells to the tumor. Killing depends on perforin and granzymes. Which cell is most likely responsible?
questions.explanation: **NK cells** are inhibited by self **MHC class I**. When a cell loses MHC class I ("**missing self**"), the inhibitory signal disappears and the NK cell kills it with **perforin and granzymes**, with no prior sensitization. **CD8+ T cells** also use perforin and granzymes, but they recognize antigen only when it is presented on MHC class I, so these tumor cells escape them.
questions.explanation_pt: As **células NK** são inibidas pelo **MHC de classe I** próprio. Quando uma célula perde o MHC de classe I (***missing self***), o sinal inibitório desaparece e a célula NK a mata com **perforina e granzimas**, sem sensibilização prévia. Os **linfócitos T CD8+** também usam perforina e granzimas, mas só reconhecem antígenos apresentados no MHC de classe I; por isso, essas células tumorais escapam deles.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old woman has had fever, flank pain and confusion for 1 day. Temperature is 39.4°C (102.9°F), blood pressure is 78/42 mm Hg and pulse is 124/min. Blood and urine cultures grow *Escherichia coli*. Her hypotension is driven by a large release of TNF-α and IL-1 from monocytes and macrophages. These cells were activated when a receptor recognized the main toxic component of the bacterial outer membrane. Which receptor is this?
questions.explanation: Lipid A is the toxic part of **lipopolysaccharide (endotoxin)**. Macrophages detect it through **TLR4** (with CD14 and MD-2), which activates **NF-κB** and a large release of TNF-α, IL-1 and IL-6, leading to **septic shock**. *E. coli* has flagella, but flagellin is sensed by **TLR5** and is not the main trigger of shock. TLR2 senses gram-positive lipoteichoic acid and lipoproteins, TLR3 senses double-stranded viral RNA, and NOD2 senses peptidoglycan fragments inside the cell.
questions.explanation_pt: O lipídio A é a parte tóxica do **lipopolissacarídeo (endotoxina)**. Os macrófagos o detectam pelo **TLR4** (com CD14 e MD-2), que ativa o **NF-κB** e uma grande liberação de TNF-α, IL-1 e IL-6, levando ao **choque séptico**. A *E. coli* tem flagelos, mas a flagelina é reconhecida pelo **TLR5** e não é o principal gatilho do choque. O TLR2 reconhece ácido lipoteicoico e lipoproteínas de gram-positivos, o TLR3 reconhece RNA viral de fita dupla e o NOD2 reconhece fragmentos de peptidoglicano dentro da célula.

notes.title: Innate immunity and complement
notes.body_md:
## Innate vs adaptive

- **Innate**: present from birth, fast (minutes to hours), not antigen-specific, **no memory**. Barriers, phagocytes, NK cells, complement and cytokines.
- **Adaptive**: T and B cells, specific, slower, with memory (see the adaptive immunity block).

## Cells

- **Neutrophils**: first responders; attracted by **C5a**, **IL-8**, LTB4 and bacterial formyl peptides; kill with the **respiratory burst** (CGD: see the immunodeficiency block).
- **Macrophages**: phagocytose, present antigen and release **IL-1**, **IL-6**, **TNF-α** and **IL-12**.
- **Dendritic cells**: carry antigen to lymph nodes and activate naive T cells; they link innate and adaptive immunity.
- **NK cells**: kill cells with low **MHC class I** and IgG-coated cells (ADCC).
- **Mast cells** and **eosinophils**: allergy and helminths.

## Pattern-recognition receptors

- Detect microbial patterns (PAMPs) and damage signals.
- **TLR4**: LPS. **TLR2**: lipoteichoic acid. **TLR3**: dsRNA. **TLR5**: flagellin. **TLR9**: CpG DNA.
- **NOD2**: cytoplasmic; peptidoglycan. **NLRP3 inflammasome**: caspase-1, IL-1β, pyroptosis.

## Complement

- Classical (antibody), lectin (mannose-binding lectin) and alternative (spontaneous C3) pathways all make a **C3 convertase**.
- **C3b**: opsonin. **C3a, C5a**: anaphylatoxins. **C5a**: neutrophil chemotaxis. **C5b-9**: membrane attack complex.
- Host regulators: **C1 inhibitor**, **DAF (CD55)**, **CD59**, factor H, factor I.
- Deficiencies: **C1q, C2, C4**: lupus-like disease. **C3**: pyogenic infections. **C5-C9**: *Neisseria*. **C1 inhibitor**: hereditary angioedema (low C4, normal C3).

## Cytokines and acute phase

- **IL-1, IL-6, TNF-α**: fever (hypothalamic **PGE2**). **IL-8**: neutrophils. **IL-12**: Th1 and NK activation. **IFN-γ**: macrophage activation. **IL-10**: anti-inflammatory.
- **IL-6** drives **CRP**, ferritin, fibrinogen and hepcidin up; albumin and transferrin down.
- **Type I interferons**: antiviral state in nearby cells.
- A massive TNF-α and IL-1 release causes **septic shock**.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Inata vs adaptativa

- **Inata**: presente desde o nascimento, rápida (minutos a horas), não específica para antígenos, **sem memória**. Barreiras, fagócitos, células NK, complemento e citocinas.
- **Adaptativa**: linfócitos T e B, específica, mais lenta, com memória (ver o bloco de imunidade adaptativa).

## Células

- **Neutrófilos**: primeira resposta; atraídos por **C5a**, **IL-8**, LTB4 e peptídeos formilados bacterianos; matam pela **explosão respiratória** (DGC: ver o bloco de imunodeficiências).
- **Macrófagos**: fagocitam, apresentam antígenos e liberam **IL-1**, **IL-6**, **TNF-α** e **IL-12**.
- **Células dendríticas**: levam antígenos aos linfonodos e ativam linfócitos T virgens; ligam a imunidade inata à adaptativa.
- **Células NK**: matam células com pouco **MHC de classe I** e células recobertas por IgG (ADCC).
- **Mastócitos** e **eosinófilos**: alergia e helmintos.

## Receptores de reconhecimento de padrões

- Detectam padrões microbianos (PAMPs) e sinais de dano.
- **TLR4**: LPS. **TLR2**: ácido lipoteicoico. **TLR3**: RNA de fita dupla. **TLR5**: flagelina. **TLR9**: DNA CpG.
- **NOD2**: citoplasmático; peptidoglicano. **Inflamassoma NLRP3**: caspase-1, IL-1β, piroptose.

## Complemento

- As vias clássica (anticorpo), das lectinas (lectina ligadora de manose) e alternativa (C3 espontâneo) formam uma **C3 convertase**.
- **C3b**: opsonina. **C3a, C5a**: anafilatoxinas. **C5a**: quimiotaxia de neutrófilos. **C5b-9**: complexo de ataque à membrana.
- Reguladores do hospedeiro: **inibidor de C1**, **DAF (CD55)**, **CD59**, fator H, fator I.
- Deficiências: **C1q, C2, C4**: doença semelhante ao lúpus. **C3**: infecções piogênicas. **C5-C9**: *Neisseria*. **Inibidor de C1**: angioedema hereditário (C4 baixo, C3 normal).

## Citocinas e fase aguda

- **IL-1, IL-6, TNF-α**: febre (**PGE2** hipotalâmica). **IL-8**: neutrófilos. **IL-12**: ativação de Th1 e NK. **IFN-γ**: ativação de macrófagos. **IL-10**: anti-inflamatória.
- A **IL-6** aumenta **PCR**, ferritina, fibrinogênio e hepcidina; reduz albumina e transferrina.
- **Interferons do tipo I**: estado antiviral nas células vizinhas.
- Uma liberação maciça de TNF-α e IL-1 causa **choque séptico**.
